\chapter{Turbine-governor models}\label{doc:model-tor}

RAMSES turbine-governor (torque) models cover the IEEE-standard diesel, gas, steam and hydro governors, a set of basic and generic ones, and four plant-specific models.

\begin{docsnote}{Usage in Dynamic Data Files}

Governor/torque models in RAMSES are defined as sub-records within a \texttt{SYNC\_MACH} block using the \texttt{TOR} keyword, followed by the model name and its parameters. They are not standalone records. The \texttt{TOR} line appears after the \texttt{EXC} (exciter) line, and the \texttt{;} at the end closes the entire \texttt{SYNC\_MACH} block.

\begin{Verbatim}
SYNC_MACH name bus FP FQ P Q SNOM Pnom H D IBRATIO
                    XT  Xl  Xd  X'd  X"d  Xq  X'q  X"q  m  n  Ra  T'do  T"do  T'qo  T"qo
              EXC model_name  param1  param2  ...
              TOR model_name  param1  param2  ... ;
\end{Verbatim}

RAMSES adds the \texttt{tor\_} prefix to the model name automatically, so both \texttt{DEGOV1} and \texttt{tor\_DEGOV1} resolve to the same model. The built-in governors (\texttt{CONSTANT}, \texttt{1ST\_ORDER}, \texttt{HYDRO\_GENERIC1}, \texttt{THERMAL\_GENERIC1}) take no prefix and are written in uppercase.

\end{docsnote}
